newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB curbs grain acceptance, misses shipping target.
newsitem.headline: CWB curbs grain acceptance, misses shipping target.

text.p: The Canadian Wheat Board said Friday it has limited acceptances of some grains under the series B sign-up after missing its shipping target for December by 800,000 tonnes as severe weather slowed movement.
"Snow slides, train derailments and the cold weather that has plagued the Prairies since early November have made it difficult for trains to get grain to the West Coast," CWB said in a statement.
Acceptance levels of 60 percent were announced for western red spring wheat, prairie spring red wheat, prairie spring white wheat and western extra strong wheat.
All western red winter, western soft white spring and western feed wheat will, however, be accepted. All barley will also be accepted. The sign-up deadline was December 31, 1996.
Durum was divided by grade with number one, two and three having a 60 percent acceptance level and number four and five a 100 percent acceptance level.

Grain not accepted will automatically roll over to Series C if farmers have chosen that option on their 1996-97 contracts. Farmers who did not chose that option have until February 28, 1997 to sign Series C contracts.
